title: Relative semiabelian Picard object and smooth Kummer comparison
statement:
Let $k$ be an algebraically closed field, let $S$ be a locally Noetherian $k$-scheme, and let $f:X\to S$ be a stable unpointed genus-$g$ family, $g\geq2$, in [def-sfb-stable-pointed-moduli-groupoids]. The identity component $N=\operatorname{Pic}^0_{X/S}$ of the relative Picard fppf sheaf is a separated smooth commutative group algebraic space of finite presentation over $S$, with geometrically connected fibres. The relative Picard sheaf is the fppf sheafification of $T\mapsto\operatorname{Pic}(X_T)/f_T^*\operatorname{Pic}(T)$; a Picard group is the group of isomorphism classes of invertible modules under tensor product [def-sc-invertible-module]. On every geometric fibre, $N$ classifies the line bundle classes of degree zero on each irreducible component and is an extension of an abelian variety by a torus. A torus is a group scheme becoming a product of copies of $\mathbf G_m$ over a separable closure; an abelian variety is a smooth proper geometrically connected group variety. Formation of $N$ commutes with base change between locally Noetherian schemes and is functorial for family isomorphisms. Let $V\subseteq S$ be the smooth-family locus. Then $N_V$ is an abelian scheme. For every integer $n\geq1$ invertible on $S$, the kernel $N[n]$ of multiplication by $n$ is an etale group algebraic space, and, on $V_{\mathrm{et}}$, the Kummer sequence gives a natural isomorphism
$$R^1(f_V)_*\mu_n\;\xrightarrow{\sim}\;N_V[n].$$
Here $\mu_n$ is the etale sheaf of units $z$ with $z^n=1$. Upon choosing a primitive $n$th root in $k$, the map $a\mapsto\zeta^a$ identifies $\underline{\mathbf Z/n\mathbf Z}$ with $\mu_n$. The displayed isomorphism is compatible with base change between locally Noetherian bases and with pullback by isomorphisms of families, using the usual cohomology pullback maps. In particular its geometric stalk at $s$ is the Kummer isomorphism $H^1(X_{\bar s},\mu_n)\simeq\operatorname{Pic}^0(X_{\bar s})[n]$. Algebraic spaces, etale cohomology and direct image are [def-trf-algebraic-space], [def-weil-pbc-etale-cohomology] and [def-weil-pbc-direct-image].

Local Deligne PDF WANTED; primary PDF read online.

proof.text: Unpack the stable-family definition: $f$ is flat and of finite presentation with nonempty connected reduced nodal geometric fibres, and is projective in the projective-bundle convention. The projective-bundle properness theorem gives properness. The universal global-sections theorem therefore supplies the canonical isomorphism $\mathcal O_T\simeq(f_T)_*\mathcal O_{X_T}$ for every base change $T\to S$. In particular $(f_T)_*\mathbf G_{m,X_T}=\mathbf G_{m,T}$: a section is a unit precisely when it has an inverse, and the structure-sheaf isomorphism preserves multiplication and $1$.

source.place: Universal structure-sheaf pushforward for proper flat geometrically reduced connected families, as recorded by lem-sc-proper-flat-global-sections; units obtained by taking invertible sections.

proof.text: Apply relative Picard representability to obtain the smooth quasi-separated locally finitely presented commutative group space $P=\operatorname{Pic}_{X/S}$. Its functor is the sheafification stated in the item. Let $D\subseteq P$ be the multidegree-zero subfunctor. The nodal multidegree-locus theorem makes it an open subgroup, quasi-compact and separated over $S$. As an open subspace of smooth $P$, $D$ is smooth and locally of finite presentation; quasi-compactness and separatedness give finite presentation. This constructs $D$ without yet identifying its fibres with the neutral components.

source.place: Section 2, printed p.135: construction of the open multidegree-zero subspace; representability and smoothness as in Stacks Tags 0D2C and 0DPK.

proof.text: Fix a geometric fibre $C=X_{\bar s}$ and its connected dual graph, with vertices $I$ and edges $E$. By the relative Picard base-change theorem, $D_{\bar s}=D\times_S\operatorname{Spec}\Omega$ is the subfunctor of $\operatorname{Pic}_{C/\Omega}$ of classes whose pullback to every normalized component has degree $\chi(\nu_Z^*L)-\chi(\mathcal O)=0$ on all geometric test fibres; by the degree decomposition of the geometric Picard theorem (degree $=\chi(L)-\chi(\mathcal O)$) this is the inverse image under $\nu^*$ of $\prod_i\operatorname{Pic}^0_{\widetilde C_i/\Omega}=\prod_iJ(\widetilde C_i)$. The normalization sequence then identifies $D_{\bar s}$ with the inverse image of $B=\prod_i J(\widetilde C_i)$ and gives $D_{\bar s}\to B$ as a smooth surjective torsor under $Q=\operatorname{coker}(\mathbf G_m^I\to\mathbf G_m^E)$. Choose a root vertex and a spanning tree. Starting at the root, rescale the vertex trivializations so that the gluing parameter along every tree edge is $1$. The remaining $|E|-|I|+1$ parameters are free, and changing the common root scalar does not affect them. This identifies $Q$ with $\mathbf G_m^{|E|-|I|+1}$. Thus the kernel is a split torus and the quotient $B$ is an abelian variety. Both are geometrically connected. A clopen partition of $D_{\bar s}$ would partition $B$ into two disjoint open subsets: smoothness makes the images open, and connected torsor fibres ensure they are disjoint. Hence $D_{\bar s}$ is connected. Since it is an open subgroup of $P_{\bar s}$, its cosets are open and its complement is open; the connected identity component cannot leave it, and its own connectedness gives $D_{\bar s}=P_{\bar s}^0$. This proves the claimed fibrewise identity and semiabelian description.

source.place: Tag 0C1M, lemma-glue-points, in its fppf normalization-sequence form; the spanning-tree calculation and connectedness argument are written here.

proof.text: The relative Picard base-change theorem identifies $P\times_SS'$ with $\operatorname{Pic}_{X_{S'}/S'}$ for every locally Noetherian base change. Under this identification the multidegree-zero condition is identical: restrictions of a class to geometric fibres and then to their normalized components have the same degrees. Thus $D\times_SS'$ is exactly the corresponding multidegree-zero subfunctor. Pullback along an isomorphism of families preserves each of those conditions and tensor products, so gives the analogous functorial identification. By the fibre identification of the previous step, $D$ is the relative identity component $N$.

source.place: Tag 0B9L, definition-picard-functor and the base-change observation following it; the multidegree condition is tested on geometric fibres.

proof.text: Over $V$ the curves are smooth, so the geometric fibres of $N_V$ are the degree-zero Picard varieties of smooth proper connected curves; these are abelian varieties by the geometric Picard theorem. The ample-line-module theorem for stable-curve Picard spaces ensures that $N_V$ is a scheme. It is smooth, separated and of finite presentation by step 2, and its fibres are nonempty connected and proper. The connected-proper-fibres criterion therefore makes $N_V\to V$ proper. Thus it is an abelian scheme, meaning a proper smooth group scheme with geometrically connected fibres. The empty smooth locus causes no exception.

source.place: Section 1.1 (properness from fibres) and Sections 4.1--4.3 (relative ample line module and scheme representability); geometric Jacobian: Stacks Tag 0BA0.

proof.text: For an integer $n\geq1$ invertible on $S$, apply the smooth-commutative-group multiplication theorem to $N$. It gives an etale map $[n]:N\to N$ and an etale group algebraic space $N[n]$, with the specified fibre-product kernel. On $V$ this is an etale scheme because $N_V$ is a scheme. No claim that $N[n]$ is finite or locally constant across singular fibres is used.

source.place: Differential argument underlying Tags 0BF5 and 0BFH, generalized by the cited input to smooth group spaces.

proof.text: For each etale $U\to V$, the exact Kummer sequence on $X_U$ gives the homomorphism $H^1(X_U,\mu_n)\to H^1(X_U,\mathbf G_m)=\operatorname{Pic}(X_U)$. Exactness of the cohomology sequence says its image is killed by $n$. Therefore the associated relative Picard class lies in $P_U[n]$ and has degree zero on every geometric component: its integer degree $d$ satisfies $nd=0$, hence $d=0$. By the multidegree criterion it lies in $N_U[n]$. The torsor description of Hilbert 90 shows that the map to Picard classes is pullback-compatible: pulling back $\operatorname{Isom}(\mathcal O,L)$ gives $\operatorname{Isom}(\mathcal O,u^*L)$. Consequently these maps form a presheaf morphism on $V_{\mathrm{et}}$. Sheafifying the source by the higher-direct-image presheaf theorem produces a specified map $\kappa:R^1(f_V)_*\mu_n\to N_V[n]$.

source.place: Tag 03PL, lemma-kummer-sequence; Tag 03P8, theorem-picard-group; Tag 03Q8, higher-direct-image presheaf description.

proof.text: At a geometric point $\bar s:\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\to V$, proper base change for the torsion sheaf $\mu_n$ identifies the source stalk with $H^1(X_{\bar s},\mu_n)$, via the usual restriction map. The stalk theorem for an etale representing scheme identifies the target stalk with $N_{\bar s}[n](\Omega)$. The universal structure-sheaf theorem applied to the proper geometrically reduced connected curve $X_{\bar s}$ gives $\Gamma(X_{\bar s},\mathcal O)^\times=\Omega^\times$. Since $\Omega$ is algebraically closed, every unit has an $n$th root. Kummer exactness and Hilbert 90 therefore identify $H^1(X_{\bar s},\mu_n)$ with $\operatorname{Pic}(X_{\bar s})[n]$. The degree decomposition of the smooth-curve Picard scheme puts every $n$-torsion class in degree zero, since $\mathbf Z$ has no $n$-torsion. Thus this is precisely $N_{\bar s}[n](\Omega)$. The map on stalks is this Kummer map, because $\kappa$ was defined by the same coefficient inclusion and line-bundle pullback. Every geometric stalk is bijective, so geometric stalk detection makes $\kappa$ an isomorphism of sheaves (and of groups).

source.place: Tag 03PL and Tag 03P8; section-pic-curves, Kummer computation in degree one. Proper base change is used only for the finite invertible-exponent sheaf mu_n.

proof.text: For any base change $S'\to S$ between locally Noetherian bases, restrict to the inverse image of $V$. A cohomology class represented on $X_U$ pulls back to its usual cohomology pullback on $X_U\times_SS'$. The coefficient maps $\mu_n\hookrightarrow\mathbf G_m$ commute with pullback of units, and the cohomology naturality theorem makes the resulting square of $H^1$ maps commute. Under Hilbert 90 its Picard class is the pullback line bundle, as the explicit torsor formula in step 7 shows. The identification of $N$ with the multidegree-zero subfunctor respects precisely that line-bundle pullback. Hence the square with $g^{-1}R^1(f_V)_*\mu_n\to R^1(f'_V)_*\mu_n$ on the left and the base-change identification of $N_V[n]$ on the right commutes after sheafification. The proper-base-change theorem gives the derived exchange isomorphism; the existing cohomology criterion gives its degree-one isomorphism, and the exchange-on-cohomology theorem identifies this with the usual degree-one map. The same calculation for a family isomorphism proves the requested isomorphism-functoriality. In particular the stalk identification in step 8 uses the ordinary cohomology pullback, not a chosen abstract group isomorphism.

source.place: Tag 03P8, torsor interpretation of Hilbert 90, with the natural Kummer sequence Tag 03PL; naturality of the usual cohomology pullback.

proof.text: If $S$ is empty, all sheaves on its etale site are uniquely isomorphic and the assertions are immediate. Otherwise choose a point of $S$: the field map from $k$ to its residue field shows that invertibility of $n$ forces $n$ to be prime to $\operatorname{char}k$. Choose a primitive $n$th root $\zeta\in k$ by the primitive-root theorem. The sections $1,\zeta,\ldots,\zeta^{n-1}$ give all roots of $T^n-1$ and are distinct in every geometric fibre; since $n$ is invertible, their pairwise differences are nonzero elements of $k$, hence units on every $k$-scheme. The Chinese remainder decomposition of $\mathcal O[T]/(T^n-1)$ therefore identifies the roots-of-unity sheaf with the constant cyclic sheaf by $a\mapsto\zeta^a$. This formula commutes with pullback. It also covers $n=1$, when both sheaves are the trivial group.

source.place: Section-pic-curves, roots-of-unity trivialization following the degree-one Kummer computation; explicit root formula.
